## Exchange before a single-block stage (`MeshBlock.forward`) {#sec-ch01-block-forward}

### Summary

A driver that steps one block calls `MeshBlock::forward` once per stage. That call runs the block's stage schedule,
whose first op on a bare block refreshes the ghost cells from the neighbours before the stage's own ops run
(@sec-ch01-stage), and then the block's global phase, the axial-momentum closure when it is on. The order matters for
a caller that edits the interior between two calls, because the edit reaches the ghosts before the next
reconstruction reads them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: run the stage schedule (stage-entry exchange first), then the axial closure.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u` and `scalar_s` with stale ghosts. Out: the same tensors advanced by one stage.

**Placement.** Once per stage, from the single-block driver.

**Activation.** Always exchanges first; no ordering switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Changes data freshness, not the stencil order; the mesh driver orders it differently.

**Evidence.** No dedicated test (missing evidence); the ownership rule is tested in @sec-ch14-timing.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlockImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}) records the step's $\Delta t$
on stage zero and hands the stage to its executor (`run_stage`), whose schedule for a bare block starts with the
stage-entry exchange as a host-exchange segment of its own
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}). With the axial-momentum closure on, it then sums
the block's closure moments, applies the solid-body increment and refills the physical ghosts (@sec-ch07).
`MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}})
exchanges the conserved hydro state and the scalar densities with interpolation on. It then re-applies every installed
wall function except outflow (the $x_1$ walls and the physical $x_2$ and $x_3$ ones) on the tangential ghost slabs the
exchange owns (the `refresh` closure, [meshblock_exchange.cpp#L153-L161](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp#L153-L161); @sec-ch14-timing), and recomputes the scalar ratios. A reflecting wall whose
tangential faces are all exchange-owned is re-applied in one call over the full extent; it writes the same slab values
and rewrites the other rows with the values they hold. A Mesh block's schedule has no stage-entry exchange: `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) runs the stages first and exchanges its blocks afterwards
(@sec-ch01-mesh). The wrapper changes when the ghosts are fresh, not the stencil order; physical boundary conditions
and cubed-sphere interpolation keep their own errors.

@fig-ch01-block-forward-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Exchange before a single-block stage. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: caller modifies interior; conserved exchange; the stage's ops; physical boundary fill; axial closure."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_block_forward_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why exchange first.** Two facts of the code decide the order.

1. The reconstruction of a stage reads ghost cells (@sec-ch04), so the ghosts must hold the neighbours' current values
   when the stage starts. The exchange op at the head of a bare block's schedule guarantees that for a single block
   ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}).
2. A driver may change the interior between two calls, for example with an operator-split source term applied on
   `hydro_u` between `forward` calls, which the comment on `forward` names
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}). With the exchange first, that change reaches
   the ghosts before the next reconstruction; with the mesh order it reaches them only after the next stage.

: Implementation anchors for the block-level forward. {#tbl-ch01-block-forward-code}

1. Run the schedule (exchange first), then the axial closure: `forward`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}).
2. Fill the layout ghosts, refresh the wall corners, recompute the scalar ratios:
   `exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
3. Compare with the mesh order, advance then exchange: `MeshImpl::forward`
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** There is nothing to configure. The whole method is
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
void MeshBlockImpl::forward(Variables &vars, double dt, int stage) {
  // Exchange BEFORE reconstruction consumes the ghosts (same count per step):
  // host-side operator-split source terms applied between forward calls
  // (e.g. condensation on hydro_u) are then synced before use, removing a
  // one-signed seam bias on the cubed sphere.
  if (stage == 0) step_dt = dt;
  // the block's schedule: the stage-entry exchange, then the stage's ops,
  // eagerly or as graphs
  _executor->run_stage(_executor_index, vars, dt, stage);
  // the global phase of a bare block, as Mesh::forward runs it over its blocks
  if (phydro->paam->closes()) {
    apply_axial_closure(vars, dt, stage,
                        global_phase_sum({axial_closure_sums()}, *_playout));
    apply_boundaries(
        vars, vars.at("hydro_u"),
        vars.count("scalar_s") ? vars.at("scalar_s") : torch::Tensor());
  }
}
```

A driver that edits `hydro_u` between calls must edit the interior only; ghost edits are overwritten by the
exchange on the next call.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| no dedicated test of the bare-block order | missing evidence | not applicable | not applicable |
| `tests/test_mesh_executor.cpp` (`test_mesh_executor.<b>`), the Mesh order | a Mesh's blocks stepped through the executor equal the local stages followed by the exchange | bitwise (`torch::equal`) | the executor changes who runs the stage, not what runs |

: Source assertions for the block-level forward. {#tbl-ch01-block-forward-tests}

No ctest isolates the bare-block order, and no report check exists for it: **missing evidence**; the ownership
rule of the exchange and the corner refresh is tested in @sec-ch14-timing. The Mesh order (stages, then the exchange)
is held bitwise by `test_mesh_executor.release`, which passed at the pin with 4 of 8 cases on CPU (the CUDA cases skip
there) and all 8 on CUDA (@sec-ch01-mesh).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The source comment on `forward` attributes a removed cubed-sphere seam bias to this placement of the exchange;
the chapter does not promote that comment to measured evidence. A regression that isolates driver-split sources between
consecutive calls is missing.
:::
